title: Captable
tagline: Compliance-aware venue for Hedera ATS securities - bids    breaching the investor cap get refused.
description:
Hedera's Asset Tokenization Studio lets issuers create and
   administer compliant securities (ERC-3643/ERC-1400) with
  KYC, freezes, and transfer restrictions — but it provides
  no venue to trade them. Cap Table is that venue: a
  compliance-aware secondary market for ATS securities
  running on Hedera testnet (chain id 296).

  Price discovery runs on Uniswap's Continuous Clearing
  Auction, deployed and used unmodified. The novel part is a
   validation hook attached to submitBid() that asks a
  question no gated auction asks today: not just "is this
  bidder permitted to hold the token?", but "if this bid
  fills to its worst case, does the resulting shareholder
  register still satisfy the issuer's compliance rules?"
  Because compliance for a security is a property of the
  whole register rather than a per-address flag, a
  permissionless auction with pro-rata fills can turn one
  large bid into dozens of small holders and silently build
  a cap table the issuer cannot legally own. Cap Table
  refuses to build that register: every bid is projected
  against the live investor-count and
  ownership-concentration limits read from the token's own
  compliance module, and bids that would breach them are
  rejected on-chain with legible, typed errors — visible in
  the UI before submission via a live chain-state preview.

  Cleared allocations settle the way a compliant security
  should: through ATS's own hold and clearing facets via a
  settlement router (the auction discovers the price, ATS
  settles the trade — delivery-versus-payment with a
  secret-reveal leg, no raw transfers). A compliance-aware
  claim path refunds any bidder whose eligibility lapsed
  between bidding and claiming, at the clearing price from a
   funded settlement reserve, so funds are never stranded. A
   Chainlink AggregatorV3-compatible NAV feed sets the
  auction floor price and a deviation band rejects
  out-of-band bids — failing open when stale so an oracle
  outage can never halt the auction.

  Everything is live on Hedera testnet: seven
  Sourcify-verified contracts (auction, hook, settlement
  router, compliance module, NAV oracle, bond), a TypeScript
   indexer serving a REST API on Railway, and an SSR web app
   on Cloudflare Workers where you can get KYC from a
  self-serve faucet, place bids, and watch them be refused
  or accepted — with every refusal recorded in a public
  ledger along with the exact compliance rule it would have
  broken.
how_its_made:
The stack is Foundry/Solidity on-chain, TypeScript off-chain, and three partner technologies stitched together through
  extension points rather than forks. Price discovery is Uniswap's Continuous Clearing Auction — deployed and used
  completely unmodified. The whole contribution hangs off the validationHook parameter CCA passes into submitBid(): a hook
   that projects the post-fill shareholder register against the issuer's compliance rules and reverts with typed errors.
  The two genuinely tricky parts there: five simultaneous bids each individually project currentHolders + 1 and all pass,
  so the settlement router keeps pending-beneficiary accounting written before submitBid (and rolled back on revert) and
  the hook is router-only — that indirection is what makes the projection sound. And it turned out ATS's balanceOf returns
   available balance while getTotalSecurityHolders counts total, so a fully-held holder reads as zero and the projection
  fails open; we closed it with a total-of helper (available + held + locked) proven by a fork test against the deployed
  bond.

  Hedera's Asset Tokenization Studio is driven through raw ABIs against its diamond facets (the published docs describe a
  newer version than the deployed v4, so every selector was resolved through DiamondLoupe first). The nastiest integration
   detail: CCA's constructor reverts unless the full token supply already sits at its address, and ATS only transfers to
  compliant addresses — so the auction's CREATE2 address had to be KYC-granted before the contract existed (getAddress → 
  grantKyc → transfer → create). Settlement uses ATS's own hold/clearing facets for DvP: a secret-hashed hold, then a
  reveal leg — with the hash stashed in the hold's data field because the documented lockHash field doesn't exist in the
  deployed version. The Chainlink integration is an AggregatorV3 NAV feed powering the floor price and a ±10% deviation
  band that fails open on staleness, wrapped in a bounded-gas staticcall so a reverting oracle can't brick bidding.


  Off-chain: a viem indexer backfills 200k blocks of auction/ATS events into Postgres (chunked, checkpointed, idempotent
  schema) and serves a REST API on Railway; the SSR frontend on Cloudflare Workers calls the hook's previewValidate
  staticcall on every keystroke so refusals render before you sign — and "Submit anyway" broadcasts refused bids with a
  fixed gas limit so the rejection is a real reverted transaction on HashScan, recorded in a public refusal ledger. 30
  Foundry tests cover the four adversarial cases; fork tests replay the live testnet deployment end-to-end, including the
  DvP hold settlement and the frozen-bidder refund path.
